lessons.title: Digital Output — LED Blink
lessons.description: Learn how to control a digital pin and blink an LED using pinMode() and digitalWrite().

circuit.notes: An Arduino Uno connected to a breadboard containing a 220Ω resistor and an LED.

info.polarityNotes: The longer leg is the anode (+), shorter leg is the cathode (–).

lessons.title: Analog Input — Potentiometer
lessons.description: Read a potentiometer, map its value, and print to the serial monitor.

circuit.notes: Lesson 2 introduces analogRead(), map(), Serial.begin(), and Serial.print().

info.notes: Turning the knob moves a wiper across a resistive track, producing 0V–5V on the middle pin.

lessons.title: Serial Monitor — Talking to Your Arduino
lessons.description: Use Serial.begin(), Serial.print(), and Serial.println() to send readable data from the Arduino to your computer.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino Tutorial (serial printing) — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: No external circuit needed — the serial monitor communicates over the USB cable.

info.notes: Serial.begin(9600) must match the monitor's baud rate or you get garbage characters.

lessons.title: Variables — Making Code Adjustable
lessons.description: Replace magic numbers with named int variables so one edit changes the whole sketch.

circuit.notes: Same LED circuit as Lesson 1 — the change is entirely in the code.

info.notes: Limits LED current below the 20mA maximum. No polarity — either direction works.

lessons.title: Conditionals — Making Decisions
lessons.description: Use if/else to change LED behavior based on the potentiometer reading.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino Tutorials (if statements) — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Combines Lesson 1's output circuit with Lesson 2's input circuit: the pot decides whether the LED is on.

info.concept: Variable resistance as a decision input
info.threshold: 512 is the midpoint of the 0–1023 ADC range
info.notes: Turn past halfway → LED on. Below halfway → LED off.
